findings.title: No LocalBusiness structured data found
findings.summary: The site has no LocalBusiness (or equivalent) JSON-LD schema markup.
findings.whyItMatters: LocalBusiness schema is how you formally tell Google: "This is a local business, here is our address, phone, hours, and category." It directly powers your Google Business Profile integration and Knowledge Panel data.
findings.recommendation: Add a LocalBusiness JSON-LD block to the homepage. Include: name, address, phone, url, openingHours, and geo coordinates. Use schema.org/LocalBusiness as the base type and a more specific subtype if applicable.
findings.impactReason: LocalBusiness schema is a key signal for Google Local Pack placement
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Reduced local pack visibility and fewer rich result features in Google Search

findings.title: No physical address detected on homepage
findings.summary: www.alaskanac.com homepage does not appear to display a business address.
findings.whyItMatters: NAP (Name, Address, Phone) consistency is a core local SEO signal. Google uses address presence to confirm local relevance and to match you with map listings.
findings.recommendation: Display your full business address in the site footer and on the homepage. Mark it up with LocalBusiness schema for extra credit.
findings.impactReason: NAP consistency across the web and homepage is a local ranking factor
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Weaker local pack signals; users can't confirm the business location

findings.title: No map embed or directions link found
findings.summary: No Google Maps embed or "Get Directions" link was detected anywhere on the site.
findings.whyItMatters: A map embed reinforces physical location signals, helps mobile users get directions instantly, and contributes to local relevance signals for Google.
findings.recommendation: Embed a Google Maps iframe on the contact page. Also add a "Get Directions" button linked to your Google Maps listing.
findings.impactReason: Embedded maps reduce friction for customers who want to visit in person
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Increased drop-off from intent-to-visit users; lost foot traffic

findings.title: No contact form found on the site
findings.summary: No lead capture form was detected on any page.
findings.whyItMatters: Not every visitor is ready to call. A contact form captures leads from visitors who prefer to inquire by email, who are outside business hours, or who want to provide details before calling.
findings.recommendation: Add a contact/inquiry form to the contact page and ideally the homepage. Keep it short: name, phone, service needed, preferred callback time.
findings.impactReason: No site-wide forms means there is no async lead capture path
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: All leads must call or email directly; visitors who prefer forms are lost

findings.title: Hero section does not clearly communicate what the business offers
findings.summary: H1 exists but is below the fold: "Air Conditioning Services in Arizona"
findings.whyItMatters: Visitors decide whether to stay or leave within seconds. A clear H1 headline stating what you do, where you do it, and what to do next dramatically reduces bounce rates from local searches.
findings.recommendation: Write an H1 that answers three questions: What do you do? Where do you serve? What should the visitor do? Example: "Expert Roof Repairs in Dallas, TX — Call for a Free Estimate."
findings.impactReason: An unclear hero message means visitors don't immediately know what the business offers
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Higher bounce rate from confused first-time visitors

findings.title: Largest Contentful Paint needs improvement (2.8s)
findings.whyItMatters: LCP is a Core Web Vitals metric used by Google for ranking. Reducing it improves both SEO and perceived load speed.
findings.recommendation: Compress the hero image, use next-gen formats (WebP/AVIF), and preload the LCP image element.
findings.impactReason: LCP is slightly above target but not severely slow

findings.title: 32% of images are missing alt text
findings.summary: 72 of 227 images across the site have no alt attribute.
findings.whyItMatters: Alt text helps Google understand image content — contributing to Google Image Search visibility and overall page relevance. It's also an accessibility requirement (ADA).
findings.recommendation: Add descriptive alt text to all images. For local businesses: include the service and location in alt text for hero images (e.g., "roof replacement Austin TX").
findings.impactReason: Missing alt text limits image search visibility and accessibility
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Missed image search traffic; minor accessibility barrier

findings.title: No About or Team page found
findings.summary: No "About Us" or team page was detected on the site.
findings.whyItMatters: Local customers often want to know who they're inviting into their home or trusting with their business. An About page humanizes your brand and builds credibility.
findings.recommendation: Add an About page that tells your story: how long you've been in business, who your team is, what makes you different, and why you care about the work you do. Include real photos of your team.
findings.impactReason: About pages build credibility but are not critical to direct conversion
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Marginally lower trust for prospects who research the business before contacting

findings.title: No gallery or portfolio page found
findings.summary: No gallery, portfolio, or before/after page was detected.
findings.whyItMatters: For trade businesses (roofers, remodelers, landscapers, etc.) and beauty services, showing your work is one of the strongest trust signals available. "Show, don't tell."
findings.recommendation: Add a gallery, portfolio, or "Our Work" page with photos of real completed jobs. For each image, add a descriptive alt text (e.g., "roof replacement Austin TX") for SEO benefit.
findings.impactReason: Gallery pages help visual businesses but are not a universal conversion factor
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Missed opportunity to showcase work quality; affects visually-driven decisions

findings.title: No visible trust signals near the top of the homepage
findings.summary: No trust signal keywords near top of page
findings.whyItMatters: Trust signals (star ratings, review counts, "Licensed & Insured") reduce hesitation for first-time visitors. Their absence makes the site feel less credible than competitors who display them prominently.
findings.recommendation: Add a trust bar below the hero section: number of Google reviews + star rating, years in business, license/insurance status, and any industry certifications.
findings.impactReason: Trust signals hidden below the fold are rarely seen before users decide to leave
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Trust content is not doing its job; conversion rate is lower than it should be

findings.title: No Google Maps embed found
findings.summary: No embedded Google Map was detected on any page of the site.
findings.whyItMatters: An embedded map reinforces the physical location to Google and helps visitors find the business — both improve local pack rankings.
findings.recommendation: Add a Google Maps embed to the contact page or homepage using the "Embed a map" option inside Google Maps.

roadmap.title: Make it immediately clear who you are and why visitors should stay
roadmap.whyItMatters: The first thing a visitor sees on your homepage determines whether they stay or leave. If there is no clear headline, photo, or trust signal above the fold (before scrolling), many visitors will bounce without ever learning about your services.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Update your homepage hero section to include: a clear headline stating what you do and where, a short sub-heading with your key selling point, a visible phone number or CTA button, and a recognizable photo (your team, your work, or your location).

roadmap.title: Tell Google exactly what kind of business you are and where you operate
roadmap.whyItMatters: Google uses structured data to display your business name, address, phone number, and hours directly in search results. Without it, you are less likely to appear in local map results and Google may mis-categorize your business.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add "LocalBusiness" structured data to your homepage. This is a small piece of code (or a plugin setting in WordPress) that gives Google your business name, type, address, phone, and opening hours in a format it can reliably read.

roadmap.title: Add your address, hours, and a map to make your location easy to find
roadmap.whyItMatters: Local customers need to know where you are, when you are open, and how to get there. If this information is missing or buried, visitors will go to a competitor whose website answers these questions immediately.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add your full address and business hours to your homepage and contact page. Embed a Google Map so visitors can get directions with one click. If you serve multiple areas, create a dedicated page for each location.

roadmap.title: Add a contact form so people can reach you any time of day
roadmap.whyItMatters: Not everyone wants to call — many visitors prefer to send a message, especially outside business hours. Without a contact form you are missing enquiries from people who would have hired you.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add a simple contact form to your contact page and ideally your homepage too. Ask only for the essentials: name, phone or email, and a brief message. Make sure form submissions arrive in an inbox you check regularly.

roadmap.title: Build visible credibility so visitors trust you before they call
roadmap.whyItMatters: Visitors decide within seconds whether a business looks trustworthy. Without reviews, credentials, photos, or an About page, many people will leave rather than risk contacting an unknown company.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add real customer reviews or testimonials to your homepage. Create an About page that introduces your team and story. Add photos of your work, vehicle, or premises. If your site is not yet on HTTPS (the padlock), ask your hosting provider to enable SSL — it is usually free.

roadmap.title: Speed up your website so visitors don't leave before it loads
roadmap.whyItMatters: A slow website frustrates visitors and hurts your Google ranking. Most people will leave a page if it takes more than 3 seconds to load, meaning you are losing leads before they even see your services.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Work with your web developer or hosting provider to compress images, reduce unnecessary scripts, and enable caching. If you use WordPress or a similar platform, a performance plugin can often fix this quickly.

roadmap.title: Add descriptions to your images so Google and screen readers can understand them
roadmap.whyItMatters: Images without alt text are invisible to Google — and to visitors using screen readers. Properly described images add keyword relevance and improve accessibility.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: For each image on your site, add a short description (alt text) explaining what the image shows. For example: "Roofing crew replacing shingles on a home in Dallas." Your CMS likely has an alt text field when you upload or edit images.
